longForm.overview:
🎎 is the emoji of festival-coded celebration flex — an imperial-pair doll display, the iconography of hinamatsuri, festival-coded energy, and the universal 'so fun 🎎' tag. Where 🎏 reads as carp-streamer-coded celebration energy and 🎐 reads as wind-chime-coded seasonal energy, 🎎 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate festival-coded charm — a 'so fun 🎎' ironic moment or a 'hinamatsuri mode 🎎' festival reveal. The doll-pair cue borrows from the imperial-display tradition and the modern festival-coded aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as celebration-coded rather than literal doll object.

In real-world usage 🎎 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate festival-coded energy. A friend sends it on a 'so fun 🎎' ironic-coded message. A family member sends it on a 'hinamatsuri mode 🎎' festival reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'celebration today 🎎' ironic-coded tag. The doll-pair cue is what makes the emoji feel festival-coded — it is not just 'japanese doll,' it is 'japanese-doll-coded celebration moment.'

What separates 🎎 from the rest of the event family is the festival-coded register. The emoji is not saying 'wind chime' (🎐), 'carp streamer' (🎏), or 'moon' (🌕). It is saying 'festival-coded celebration,' which carries a specific hinamatsuri tradition. That is why 🎎 travels especially well on 'so fun' tags, festival-coded reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with imperial-pair energy.
